newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Bargain hunters boost Australia stocks by end.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Bargain hunters boost Australia stocks by end.

text.p: SPI futures 2227 +9 US 30yr cl 7.02 -0.02
*Stocks hold most gains by close, bargain hunters lift miners off lows, industrials firm. Turnover 224.40 million, value A$633.73 million, 927 traded, 336 steady, 290 up, 301 down
The Australian share market closed higher on Tuesday, keeping a firm grasp on gains that had looked unlikely at the start of the day.
At 4.10 p.m. (0610 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 9.5 points higher at 2228.7.
The September share price index was nine points up at 2227 and at a 1.7 point discount to the underlying index.
Broker said bargain hunters had buoyed the bourse after an initial selldown, driven by weaker metals prices ovenight, quickly petered out and investors went looking for value.
"We had solid buying this afternoon," said a Sydney broker.
"The selling dried up early and the bargain hunters were about. The leaders have been well marked down recently."
Turnover at A$633 million was solid rather than spectacular, with investors anticipating greater activity after the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meets on Tuesday night.
"I would expect more action tomorrow after the FOMC meets tonight. Some are holding back (until then)," the broker said.
Oil and gas major Santos saw its shares jump to a six year high after announcing a new oil and gas find in Queenland, its second in the Cooper/Eromanga Basin in the last week.

Beverages group CC-Amatil, transport and logistics group Brambles and telecoms, transport and healthcare group Mayne Nickless found support as investors targetted growth stocks after a flat few days for the industrial sector.
Falls just shaded rises, while about 36 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures saw good activity levels as traders covered positions when the market turned early. Options trade was more active than Monday but remained thin.
Total options traded 41,204 (34,194)
Trade in September SPI contracts totalled 9,251 (6,446)

In other local markets, Australian bonds suffered another lacklustre trading session as investors generally stood aside ahead of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting on Tuesday night, and where a policy tightening could be endorsed.
By 5.00 p.m. (0700 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.93 percent, down 0.02 from Monday's close.
The Australian dollar was hovering around US$0.7900 in late trading as the waiting game ahead of the (FOMC) meeting later today neared an end.
By 5.00 p.m (0700 GMT), the unit was quoted at US$0.7890/95 with traders saying Japanese selling had given it a softer tone.
